Effective waste management is a fundamental part of Choksi Heraeus Private Limited’s commitment to environmental stewardship, workplace safety, and strict regulatory compliance. The company has established structured waste handling practices across its refining, manufacturing, laboratory, and maintenance operations, ensuring responsible management of both hazardous and non-hazardous materials.

Waste Segregation at Source

This SOP establishes a comprehensive and standardized waste management procedure at Choksi Heraeus Private Limited. It ensures proper segregation, classification, storage, handling, transportation, recycling, and disposal of waste, with a strong emphasis on environmental sustainability, employee safety, and compliance with applicable Indian environmental regulations, including those mandated by the Pollution Control Board and other relevant authorities.

This SOP applies to all refining, manufacturing, research, and support functions at Choksi Heraeus Private Limited, covering the complete waste lifecycle from generation and segregation to final disposal or recovery. It includes provisions for process waste, laboratory waste, maintenance waste, administrative waste, and hazardous materials, managed in accordance with Indian regulations and globally recognized best practices.

A centralized Waste Stream Register is maintained at the facility, overseen by the EHS Officer in coordination with respective department heads.
The register captures the following details:
Source of generation (e.g., refining unit, laboratory, MEE Plant, warehouse, administration)
Waste type and classification (hazardous, recyclable, precious metal-bearing, organic, etc.)

Waste segregation is carried out at the source using color-coded bins as per CPCB guidelines, with special provisions for precious metal-bearing residues to ensure traceability.
Training programs on waste identification, handling, and regulatory compliance are conducted annually for all relevant employees and contractors.

Segregation as per Waste Types

Waste generated at Choksi Heraeus Private Limited is systematically categorized and segregated at the source to prevent cross-contamination, ensure traceability of precious metal-bearing residues, and maintain compliance with national environmental regulations. Clearly labelled, color-coded bins and secure storage containers are used across the facility, and all employees receive training in proper waste identification, segregation, and handling procedures.

Minimizing Cross-Contamination

Separation of Hazardous Waste: Chemical, solvent, and precious metal-bearing waste are strictly separated to prevent chemical reactions, safety hazards, or loss of valuable material.
Sealed Containers for Special Waste: Waste such as spent solvents, contaminated lab reagents, and MEE Plant sludge are stored in sealed, leak-proof containers with secondary containment.
Monitoring by Supervisors: Department supervisors and EHS personnel conduct regular checks to ensure proper segregation practices are consistently implemented.

Handling Special Waste Streams

Chemical Residues & Spent Solvents: Collected separately in designated hazardous waste containers and managed in compliance with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016.
Precious Metal-Bearing Waste: Stored securely in locked containers, tracked through waste registers, and processed through authorized recovery or refining channels to ensure zero loss.
E-Waste: Obsolete electronic equipment, batteries, and circuit boards are segregated at source and stored in a designated e-waste zone. Disposal is carried out only through CPCB-authorized e-waste recyclers as per the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.

Choksi Heraeus Private Limited adopts a proactive, multi-tiered approach to minimize waste generation throughout its refining, laboratory, and production activities. Aligned with India’s environmental regulations and global sustainability standards, the company prioritizes source reduction, material recovery, reuse, and process optimization over disposal, with a focus on minimizing environmental impact, safeguarding resources, and enhancing circularity through precious metal recovery.

Promotion of Material Reuse and Recovery

Recoverable Materials

Periodic waste stream audits are conducted to identify recyclable and recoverable materials across refining and laboratory operations. Key recoverable materials include:

Precious Metal-Bearing Residues: Dust, sweeps, filter bags, ash, and polishing waste are systematically collected and reprocessed to recover valuable metals.
Chemical Reagents & Solutions: Where feasible, solvents and process solutions are purified and reused in non-critical laboratory or production processes.
Packaging Materials: Cartons, pallets, drums, and plastic wraps are segregated for reuse or recycling.
Scrap Metals & Defective Components: Off-spec products and scrap metal from production are repurposed or sent to authorized recyclers for recovery.

Recovery and Collection Steps

Collection Points: Designated containers and secured collection points are placed in refining, laboratory, and warehouse areas.
Segregation and Sorting: Materials are manually and mechanically segregated under strict supervision, with special protocols for precious metal-bearing residues.
Employee Engagement: Regular training and awareness programs are conducted to ensure employees recognize recoverable materials and understand their role in waste reduction.

Recovery Process and Optimization

Precious Metal-Bearing Residues: Collected and refined through in-house recovery processes or sent to authorized refining partners.
Chemical Reagents & Solvents: Treated for safe reuse in low-priority or test batches, reducing chemical waste.
Packaging Materials: Stored for internal reuse in logistics, with damaged items sent to authorized recyclers.
Scrap Metals & Defective Products: Segregated and repurposed as test samples or recycled through approved vendors.

In addition to reuse and recovery, Choksi Heraeus implements process improvements to minimize waste at the point of generation, including:

Right-First-Time (RFT) Operations: Stringent quality controls in refining and laboratory processes reduce reworks, rejections, and loss of material.
Automated Dosing & Chemical Controls: Precision dosing systems minimize overuse of chemicals, lowering hazardous waste generation.
Lean Manufacturing Practices: Eliminate inefficiencies such as idle inventory, overproduction, and unnecessary handling, reducing process-related waste.
Process Yield Optimization: Continuous monitoring of refining yields ensures maximum recovery of precious metals, reducing material losses.
Batch Optimization: Careful production planning maximizes equipment utilization and minimizes partial or inefficient processing cycles.

Storage Procedures

Hazardous Waste

Containers for Hazardous Waste

Hazardous waste is stored in leak-proof, sealed, and chemically compatible containers to prevent leaks and contamination. These containers are chosen based on the specific chemical properties of the waste to ensure maximum safety. All containers remain securely closed except during waste loading activities.

Labeling of Hazardous Waste Containers

To ensure safe storage, handling, and disposal of hazardous waste, Choksi Heraeus Pvt. Ltd. follows mandatory labeling procedures in line with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, issued by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and enforced by the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB).

Labeling Specifications

Material: Labels are made of chemical-resistant and weatherproof material, suited for high-temperature and humid environments typical to Rajasthan.
Size: Minimum dimensions of 4 x 6 inches, visible from at least 2 meters.
Font & Contrast: Bold text in English. Font size: minimum 12-point for key information. High contrast colors (e.g., black on white or red) for clear readability.
Adhesion: Labels must be securely affixed to resist heat, moisture, and chemical exposure.
Placement: Affixed to the upper front portion of each container for easy visibility during inspection and handling.
Label Must Include: “Hazardous Waste” and relevant hazard symbol(s); Waste category and physical state (liquid, sludge, etc.); Date of generation; Generator’s name and contact details (Choksi Heraeus pvt. Ltd.); Emergency response information or hazard classification code.

Information Included on the Label

Each hazardous waste container includes the following:

Waste Type
Waste Code
Date of Generation
Quantity
Signal Word: DANGER
Hazard Statement: Flammable liquid and vapor. Toxic if inhaled.
Handling Instructions: Keep tightly closed. Store away from heat and flame.
Generator Name: Choksi Heraeus pvt. Ltd.
Contact Person: EHS Manager
Contact Details: +91- 7665454899| ehs.udr@ravindraheraeus.com

Inspection and Maintenance

Labels are reviewed during internal waste audits to ensure clarity and regulatory compliance.
Damaged or unreadable labels are immediately replaced.
Any unlabeled containers are promptly flagged and relabeled by trained personnel.

Designated Storage Areas for Hazardous Waste

Hazardous waste is stored in clearly marked, secure areas away from operational zones.
Access is restricted to trained personnel only.
The storage zone features impervious flooring, bunds, proper ventilation, and fire suppression systems.
Regular inspections are conducted for leaks or container damage, with spill kits and emergency plans in place.

Non-Hazardous Waste Storage

Containers: Non-hazardous waste is stored in standard, non-leaking containers. These containers are not required to meet the same stringent specifications as hazardous waste containers but must still be durable enough to withstand normal handling conditions.
Labeling: Non-hazardous waste is not required to have detailed hazard labels, containers are clearly labeled to indicate the waste type (e.g., packaging waste, office waste).
Storage Areas: Non-hazardous waste is stored in designated collection areas that are separate from hazardous waste storage zones. These areas should be kept clean and organized to avoid cross-contamination with hazardous or recyclable waste.
Spill Containment: Spill containment materials are available near storage areas to address any accidental spills promptly.

Recyclable Waste Storage

Containers: Recyclable waste (e.g., plastics, paper, metals) are stored in separate bins marked clearly with the type of material.
Sorting: Recycling bins are sorted according to the type of material (e.g., separate bins for plastics, paper, metal, and glass) to facilitate easy and efficient recycling.
Storage Area: Recyclables are stored in areas that is dry, clean, and away from potential contamination sources. The area is well-organized to facilitate easy access and transportation to recycling facilities.

Handling Procedures

Hazardous Waste Handling

PPE: Mandatory use of gloves, goggles, masks/respirators, and protective gear based on hazard level.
Training: Staff receive regular training on safe handling, segregation, and emergency protocols.
Spill Control: Secondary containment is used. Any spill is managed as per Choksi Heraeus Pvt. Ltd. spill response plan.

Non-Hazardous Waste Handling

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): While non-hazardous waste handling does not typically require specialized PPE, workers should wear gloves and other general protective equipment to prevent minor injuries.
Handling Instructions: Non-hazardous waste should be handled with care to avoid contamination with hazardous or recyclable materials. The waste should be placed directly into designated containers to ensure segregation is maintained.
Safety Considerations: The handling area for non-hazardous waste should be kept clean and organized to ensure safe handling and quick access to storage or disposal facilities.

Recyclable Waste Handling

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Employees should wear gloves and any other PPE deemed necessary to handle recyclables safely.
Sorting: Employees must follow proper sorting instructions to ensure that recyclable materials are separated by type (e.g., plastics, paper, cloth) and are not contaminated by non-recyclable or hazardous materials.
Handling Procedures: Recyclables should be handled carefully to prevent breakage and must be compacted if needed to reduce volume and prepare them for transportation.

Transportation Procedures

Choksi Heraeus Private Limited ensures that hazardous waste is transported with the highest standards of safety, compliance, and traceability. All activities are performed in accordance with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, and the applicable Rajasthan Pollution Control Board (RPCB) guidelines.

Hazardous Waste Transportation

Licensed Contractors

All hazardous waste is transported exclusively by CPCB and SPCB-authorized hazardous waste transport contractors.
Contractors are required to hold valid transport licenses, vehicle fitness certificates, and personnel training certifications as per Rule 19 of the 2016 Hazardous Waste Rules.
Service-level agreements ensure contractors adhere to both national and state-level environmental laws and submit documentation before each dispatch.

Container Sealing and Vehicle Safety

Pre-Dispatch Inspection: All hazardous waste containers undergo visual and physical inspection by the EHS Officer to ensure they are undamaged, leak-proof, and compliant with prescribed specifications.
Container Specifications: Constructed of HDPE or corrosion-resistant steel. Equipped with tamper-evident lids and secure locking systems. Labeled in accordance with Schedule II of the 2016 Rules, including waste category, generation date, and hazard symbols in English.
Transport Vehicle Safety Features: Equipped with spill containment trays, absorbent lining, and segregation compartments. Clearly marked with “HAZARDOUS WASTE” placards, including appropriate UN hazard codes and color-coded labels. Vehicle body inspected for container stability and tie-down security prior to dispatch.

Documentation and Regulatory Compliance

Each shipment is accompanied by a full set of documentation as required under Rule 19 of the Hazardous Waste Rules and SPCB SOPs:

Form 10 – Hazardous Waste Manifest: Contains generator details, transporter information, quantity, physical state, and final disposal location. Signed by the generator (Choksi Heraeus Private Limited), transporter, and TSDF upon completion.
Transport Authorization Certificate: Verified copy of contractor’s waste transport approval issued by the SPCB.
Safety Data Sheets (SDS): Specific to the hazardous material being transported. Includes chemical composition, physical properties, hazards, first aid measures, and firefighting precautions.

Emergency Preparedness and Response

Transport vehicles are equipped and staffed to handle emergency situations involving hazardous waste.

On-Board Emergency Kit Includes: Absorbent pads, neutralizing agents, spill containment socks, waste collection bags. Complete set of PPE: gloves, masks, aprons, goggles, face shields. Fire extinguisher and first-aid kit.
Personnel Training: Drivers and accompanying staff are trained in: classification and handling of hazardous waste under Indian rules; on-site spill containment, evacuation procedures, and safe zone establishment; immediate communication protocols with SPCB, local authorities, and emergency responders; first aid and hazard-specific response techniques.
Emergency Plan Adherence: Transport staff must follow Choksi Heraeus Pvt. Ltd. Emergency Response Plan (ERP) including: rapid isolation of spill zone; notification to Environmental Compliance Officer and SPCB; activation of third-party emergency cleanup services, if necessary.

Transportation Execution and Post-Delivery Verification

Route Planning and Pre-Dispatch Checks: Transported via pre-approved, low-risk routes identified to minimize environmental and human health risks. Vehicles undergo pre-departure inspections for: container integrity; proper label display; documentation readiness; secure cargo placement.
Segregation of Incompatibles: Flammable, reactive, or corrosive substances are stored separately within the transport vehicle, using CPCB-compliant segregation barriers.
Delivery and Reconciliation at TSDF: On reaching the authorized Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facility (TSDF): waste is unloaded under supervision; quantity and type are verified against manifest entries; any discrepancies are documented, reported, and investigated. Form 10 is updated, signed, and one copy is returned to Choksi Heraeus Private Limited for records.

Non-Hazardous Waste Transportation

Transportation Vehicles: Non-hazardous waste is transported using regular vehicles designed to carry bulk waste. These vehicles should be equipped with secure and leak-proof containers to prevent contamination during transit.
Route Planning: Non-hazardous waste should be transported directly to disposal or recycling facilities without unnecessary detours to minimize time and risk of spillage.

Recyclable Waste Transportation

Designated Vehicles: Recyclable materials should be transported in vehicles dedicated to recycling operations to ensure they are not contaminated by other waste streams.
Proper Sealing: Recyclable materials should be securely stored in containers to prevent leakage, breakage, or contamination during transportation.

Hazardous Waste Treatment and Disposal

Choksi Heraeus Private Limited is committed to minimizing the environmental and human health impacts of hazardous substances generated during production through the implementation of specialized treatment protocols and safe disposal systems. These procedures are aligned with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) directives.

Specialized In-House Treatment Techniques

Hazardous waste generated during Choksi Heraeus’ precious metal refining and allied manufacturing processes is treated on-site using customized methods appropriate to its type and risk level:

Neutralization Units: Acidic and alkaline effluents are neutralized to safe pH levels prior to storage, treatment, or disposal.
Sludge Solidification: Sludge from wastewater treatment plant containing chemicals and metal traces is stabilized with binding agents (such as saturated lime) to form a non-leachable, solid mass suitable for secure landfilling.
Solvent Recovery and Segregation: Valuable spent solvents are segregated, stored, and sent for recovery, minimizing environmental load and supporting circular use.
Container Cleaning Units: Used drums and containers are triple-rinsed and stored in designated areas for return to suppliers.

All activities are overseen by trained Environment, Health & Safety (EHS) personnel with regular monitoring to ensure compliance and operational safety.

Safe and Compliant Disposal

After treatment, hazardous waste is dispatched to CPCB/SPCB-authorized Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities (TSDFs):

steps.heading: Material Consumption Reduction by process optimization

body.text: Process Innovation for Precise Material Use. Automated dosing and feeding systems are deployed to ensure exact quantities of iron ore, alloying agents, reducing agents, and binders are used in production. Advanced process control in reduction furnaces, milling, and atomization prevents the overuse of raw materials and energy. Real-time monitoring with sensors and data analytics allows adjustment of process parameters without affecting powder quality or particle size distribution. Closed-loop recovery systems are implemented to capture and reuse heat, process gases, and metallic residues wherever feasible, improving sustainability and resource efficiency.

Reintegration of Recovered Input Materials. Metallic residues such as fine dust from milling, filter cake from dust collectors, and by-products from sieving and classification are systematically collected, treated, and reintroduced into the production cycle after quality verification. These recovered materials are blended back into new batches, reducing reliance on virgin ore and raw materials by up to 20–25%. This practice lowers raw material costs, minimizes environmental impact, and supports Choksi Heraeus’s commitment to circular economy principles.

Enhanced Production Planning and Process Scheduling. Optimized production planning ensures that batch sizes are aligned with customer demand and furnace capacity, minimizing excess production and material losses. Efficient scheduling reduces the number of machine changeovers and cleaning cycles, thereby cutting down the use of lubricants, cleaning chemicals, and purge materials. Sequencing of production runs is planned to minimize cross-contamination between different powder grades, reducing reprocessing needs. These measures streamline operations, enhance resource utilization, and improve overall material efficiency.

steps.heading: Integration of Eco-Friendly materials and safer alternative substances

body.text: Choksi Heraeus has implemented a comprehensive approach to reduce waste generation and environmental impact by integrating eco-friendly raw materials, safer chemical substitutes, and certified inputs across its manufacturing processes. The following practices are embedded in operations:

Recyclable and Sustainable Metal Inputs: Wherever feasible, recycled base metals and alloys are prioritized in production. Inputs are sourced with traceability to ensure reduced environmental footprint and support circular economy principles.
Low-Toxicity Processing Agents: Fluxes, lubricants, and other processing chemicals used in refining, atomization, and finishing are selected based on biodegradability, non-toxicity, and absence of hazardous components such as heavy metals, cyanides, or persistent organic pollutants, thereby minimizing MEE Plant sludge and hazardous waste.
Eco-Friendly Surface Treatments: Preference is given to surface treatments that use water-based and low-VOC solutions instead of solvent-based coatings, reducing atmospheric emissions and simplifying effluent treatment.
High-Efficiency Additives: Alloying and binding agents with high conversion efficiency are employed to ensure maximum utilization during processing, minimizing unreacted residues and material loss.
Certified and Compliant Inputs: All raw materials, additives, and auxiliary chemicals are procured only from vendors who comply with recognized standards such as REACH, RoHS, and ISO 14001, ensuring sustainability and safe end-of-life management.
Vendor Qualification and Monitoring: Suppliers are approved based on strict environmental and safety criteria, including evidence of reduced waste-intensive profiles. Vendors are re-assessed bi-annually to ensure sustained compliance and encourage adoption of safer alternatives.
Internal Waste Profiling: Material inputs undergo periodic waste profiling in collaboration with the MEE team to validate biodegradability, recyclability, and impact on effluent quality, ensuring that only environmentally compatible inputs are allowed in the production cycle.

steps.heading: Adoption of Safer alternative & less-hazardous Substances

body.text: Identification of Hazardous Inputs. A quarterly review of all process chemicals, fluxes, reagents, and surface-treatment agents is conducted to identify substances falling under ZDHC MRSL, EU REACH Annex XVII, and BIS safety lists that may pose risks to worker safety, effluent treatment, or waste generation.
Substitution with Greener Alternatives

Solvents & Degreasers: Petroleum-based cleaning solvents have been replaced with water-based, biodegradable degreasers that reduce VOC emissions.
Surfactants: Conventional surfactants used in cleaning are substituted with plant-derived, biodegradable surfactants with proven compatibility in metal-processing applications.
Pickling & Bleaching Agents: Acid-intensive pickling systems are gradually replaced with enzyme-assisted and peroxide-based treatments that minimize hazardous by-products.
Surface Coatings & Additives: Heavy-metal stabilizers and high-toxicity additives are phased out and replaced with low-toxicity,
Lubricants & Softeners: Synthetic cationic lubricants are substituted with bio-based formulations (soy/palm derived) that are fully biodegradable and easier to treat in the MEE Plant.

Pre-Approval and Testing. All alternative substances undergo performance trials for compatibility with metallurgical processes (powder quality, purity, sintering, surface finish) before approval. Only inputs with third-party certifications where applicable, or supplier MSDS with eco-safety compliance are cleared for use. Operators are trained prior to implementation of each substitution.
Mercury Non-Use. CHPL strictly prohibits the procurement, storage, or use of mercury and mercury-based compounds across all operations. This policy is aligned with:

Minamata Convention on Mercury (global treaty to protect human health and the environment).
Indian environmental regulations (Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016).
Customer-specific Restricted Substances Lists (RSLs).
To ensure compliance:

Supplier declarations and MSDS are verified quarterly to confirm that no raw material contains mercury traces.
Internal audits and chemical inventory checks include a specific “mercury-free” verification step.
Employees are trained on the health, environmental, and regulatory risks of mercury to reinforce zero-tolerance use.

Monitoring and Recordkeeping. Monthly review of effluent treatment data, solvent consumption logs, and chemical supplier MSDS ensures substituted substances are consistently applied and continue to meet safety and environmental performance benchmarks. Full audit trails are maintained for regulatory and customer verification.

steps.heading: Reducing Hazardous By-Product Formation and Toxicity

body.text: Choksi Heraeus has implemented proactive measures to minimize the generation of hazardous by-products during metal processing and ensure their safe management:

Use of low-toxicity fluxes, binders, and processing chemicals has replaced conventional inputs to reduce emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), heavy metals, and other hazardous pollutants.
Process conditions such as furnace temperature, atmosphere, and pH in wet treatments are carefully controlled to prevent the formation of Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) and other toxic by-products.
Advanced filtration, dust collection, and chemical recovery systems are installed to capture and reclaim residual particulates, solvents, and metallic compounds before they enter air or water streams.
All hazardous wastes, including spent solvents, oily residues, and contaminated sludges, are treated and disposed of only through government-authorized facilities, in strict compliance with national environmental regulations.

blocks.text: To define a comprehensive energy management procedure that enhances operational efficiency, reduces environmental impact, and supports long-term sustainability across Choksi Heraeus’ refining, recycling, and advanced material manufacturing operations.
This procedure applies to all energy-consuming processes and equipment at Choksi Heraeus, including manufacturing machinery, lighting, HVAC systems, thermal equipment, and digital infrastructure.
The following procedures reflect the established practices implemented to enhance energy efficiency, optimize resource utilization, and minimize environmental impact in our operations.

body.text: To enhance energy efficiency and reduce overall electricity consumption, Choksi Heraeus has implemented the following equipment and process-level optimization strategies:

substeps.text: Upgrade to Energy-Efficient Equipment: High-Efficiency Crucible Furnaces & Melting Units. Precious metal melting operations at Choksi Heraeus rely heavily on crucible furnaces and induction melting units. These systems are progressively upgraded to high-efficiency induction-based heating technologies that reduce thermal losses, optimize heat transfer, and maintain uniform temperature distribution. Insulation materials with low thermal conductivity are introduced in crucibles and furnace linings to retain heat, thereby reducing electricity and fuel usage. Process Reactors & Refining Units: Refining reactors and chemical processing units are equipped with energy-efficient heating mantles, jacketed vessels, and digital temperature control systems, minimizing overconsumption of energy during reactions. Material Handling, Pumps, and Ventilation Systems: Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) and inverter-based motors are integrated into pumps, air compressors, and fume extraction systems to ensure energy usage is dynamically regulated according to real-time process requirements, rather than running at full load continuously. Smart automation ensures that ventilation and dust collection systems in polishing and casting areas operate on demand, thereby minimizing idle energy consumption. Replacement of Obsolete Machinery: A structured equipment replacement program is in place, where outdated, energy-intensive furnaces, compressors, and polishing machines are systematically replaced with internationally certified energy-rated models that comply with ISO 50001 energy management guidelines. Benchmarking against global Heraeus Group standards ensures alignment with best practices in energy efficiency, sustainability, and operational safety.

Energy Performance Monitoring and Preventive Maintenance: Energy meters and monitoring systems are connected to critical production and laboratory equipment to provide real-time data on energy consumption and anomalies. Data is reviewed weekly by the engineering and EHS teams to identify energy inefficiencies and corrective measures. Preventive maintenance schedules are aligned with energy performance data to: maintain optimal efficiency of refining, melting, and chemical processing units; prevent excessive energy use caused by mechanical wear, leakages, or system inefficiencies; extend the life of critical equipment, reducing both operational costs and the environmental footprint of replacements.

body.text: Choksi Heraeus has modernized its facility-wide lighting infrastructure to optimize energy efficiency, reduce operational costs, and maintain high standards of workplace safety and illumination across laboratories, production floors, storage areas, and administrative offices.

substeps.text: LED Lighting Retrofit: Legacy fluorescent, incandescent, and halogen fixtures have been systematically replaced with high-efficiency LED systems across all operational and non-operational zones. LEDs are selected based on lumen-per-watt efficiency, color accuracy (CRI), and extended service life, ensuring optimum visibility for precision work with reduced power consumption. This transition has delivered measurable reductions in electricity use and minimized maintenance downtime, supporting the company’s sustainability targets.

Motion and Daylight Sensors: Motion sensors are deployed in low-occupancy zones such as corridors, restrooms, and auxiliary storage rooms to ensure lighting is activated only when required. Daylight sensors are installed in areas with natural light access, automatically adjusting or switching off artificial lighting when daylight levels are sufficient. These sensor-based systems collectively reduce unnecessary energy consumption during non-peak hours and daylight-rich periods.

Zonal and Smart Lighting Controls: The facility is divided into independent lighting zones based on activity areas and occupancy schedules. For example: production zones operate on extended schedules; storage and loading bays follow reduced lighting cycles. Smart control systems use programmable timers and real-time data to dynamically adjust lighting intensity and duration based on occupancy sensors, time-of-day settings, and natural light availability. Emergency and exit lighting systems remain exempt from automated controls to ensure continuous safety compliance.

body.text: Automated Monitoring and Performance Tracking: The solar PV systems installed at Choksi Heraeus facilities are integrated with advanced monitoring software that continuously captures and analyzes: real-time power generation and cumulative energy yield; system efficiency metrics and long-term panel performance trends; deviations from standard operating parameters, including voltage fluctuations and output irregularities; automatic alerts in case of anomalies, ensuring rapid diagnostics and corrective action.

substeps.text: Preventive Maintenance and Inspection Schedule: Solar Panel Cleaning: Panels are cleaned at defined intervals (monthly) to remove dust, industrial residues, or organic matter that may obstruct light absorption. Component Inspection: Routine inspections are conducted for inverters and junction boxes (checked for faults, overheating, or signs of internal wear); cabling and connectors (examined for physical damage, corrosion, or loose connections); mounting structures (assessed for structural integrity, rust, and anchoring stability).

Fault Response and Corrective Maintenance: Any deviations or underperformance identified by the monitoring system are immediately reported to the maintenance team. On-site diagnostics are carried out to identify issues such as malfunctioning inverters or failed modules; faulty connectors, wiring damage, or panel shading. Identified faults are promptly addressed through repair or component replacement using certified parts, ensuring minimal system downtime.

Health, Safety, and Risk Control Measures: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): All personnel engaged in maintenance activities are required to wear appropriate PPE, including electrical-grade gloves, helmets, eye protection, non-conductive footwear, and harnesses for rooftop access. Lockout/Tagout (LOTO): Strict LOTO procedures are followed before performing maintenance to eliminate the risk of electrical shock or unintended activation. Fire Safety Compliance: Electrical installations are maintained in accordance with fire safety norms. Appropriate fire extinguishers (Class C-rated) are readily available near control panels and inverter stations.

Documentation, Recordkeeping, and Compliance: Comprehensive records are maintained covering daily, weekly, and monthly energy production data; scheduled maintenance, cleaning logs, and fault resolutions; system performance trends and deviation reports. Regulatory Compliance: Operations align with the Electricity Act, 2003, CEA Safety Regulations, and relevant Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) for solar installations. Annual internal audits are conducted to ensure continued compliance and system optimization.

steps.heading: Heat Recovery and Thermal Energy Optimization

body.text: Choksi Heraeus has adopted advanced waste heat recovery and thermal optimization measures across its metallurgical and process operations to maximize energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions.

substeps.text: Heat Recovery from Process Equipment: High-temperature operations in furnaces and metal treatment units release substantial waste heat. This residual heat is captured through plate and shell-type heat exchangers installed on exhaust and discharge systems. The recovered heat is redirected to preheat process water, combustion air, and raw material streams, thereby reducing the overall energy input needed.

Thermal Insulation of Pipelines: All steam lines, hot water pipelines, and molten metal transfer channels are insulated with high-grade, heat-resistant materials. Insulation minimizes thermal losses during transfer, stabilizes operating temperatures, and reduces the frequency of heating cycles. Enhanced insulation efficiency contributes to consistent process performance and reduced operational costs.

Reduced Dependence on External Energy Sources: By reusing internally generated heat, the system reduces reliance on external heating systems such as additional fuel-based heaters or grid power, is minimized. This results in lower energy consumption, reduced fossil fuel usage, and a measurable decrease in carbon dioxide emissions. The initiative directly supports Choksi Heraeus Private Limited’ sustainability and decarbonization goals, aligning with both internal targets and external environmental compliance frameworks.

body.text: To comply with environmental regulations and reduce climate impact, Choksi Heraeus implements the following measures for systems containing refrigerants and other F-gases.

substeps.text: Refrigerant Management: All HVAC and cooling systems at Choksi Heraeus are operated with low-global-warming-potential (low-GWP) refrigerants such as R-1234yf and R-744 (Carbon Dioxide). Preventive maintenance programs are in place to detect and eliminate leaks, minimizing F-gas emissions and ensuring compliance with international standards.
High-Efficiency HVAC Units: Conventional air conditioning units are gradually replaced with inverter-based, energy-rated models that automatically adjust compressor speed to match cooling demand.

Zoned Cooling Systems: Cleanrooms, laboratories, and process control areas are equipped with smart zoning systems, ensuring cooling is delivered only where needed instead of running at full load across the facility.

Servicing and Maintenance: Only certified technicians handle refrigerants, ensuring correct charging and recovery practices. Maintenance logs are maintained for each unit, recording refrigerant type, quantity, leak test results, and service history. Technicians perform scheduled leak tests and system audits on all refrigerant-based equipment, with automated alerts for anomalies in pressure or performance to ensure early detection of inefficiencies.

body.text: Recognizing the growing energy demand of IT systems, Choksi Heraeus has implemented the following measures to reduce consumption in server rooms, data storage, and IT-related infrastructure:

substeps.text: Energy-Efficient Hardware: All new IT assets, including servers, data storage systems, and networking devices, are procured with Energy Star or equivalent certifications, ensuring lower energy use per processing capacity. A structured hardware refresh cycle is maintained, where outdated, high-consumption servers and devices are replaced with modern, energy-rated models.

Virtualization and Cloud Optimization: Server virtualization is applied across critical applications to reduce the number of physical servers in operation, improving efficiency. Non-sensitive and non-critical workloads are progressively migrated to cloud service providers with verifiable commitments to renewable energy usage. Centralized workload management tools balance IT demand dynamically, preventing unnecessary over-provisioning.

Energy Monitoring and Smart Controls: IT infrastructure is continuously monitored using Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) as the benchmark to track and improve efficiency. Idle systems are set to automated low-power states or shutdown, while workstations and peripherals use intelligent power management settings. Real-time dashboards enable the IT team to identify anomalies and optimize consumption trends.

Lifecycle and End-of-Life Management: Obsolete IT hardware is phased out systematically and processed through certified e-waste vendors to ensure secure disposal. Data destruction protocols (such as secure wiping and degaussing) are followed before hardware is handed over for recycling. Where possible, refurbished equipment is redirected for secondary use in non-critical operations before end-of-life disposal.

body.text: Carbon Footprint Calculation: Choksi Heraeus Private Limited undertakes comprehensive carbon footprint assessments to quantify and manage its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The calculation process follows internationally recognized standards, primarily the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol, ensuring consistency, accuracy, and global comparability. Emissions are systematically categorized into Scope 1 (direct emissions from sources owned or controlled by the company, such as emissions from boilers, generators, and manufacturing equipment); Scope 2 (indirect emissions from the consumption of purchased electricity, steam, or other forms of imported energy used in production and administrative operations); Scope 3 (other indirect emissions that occur in the value chain, including emissions from upstream activities such as raw material transportation and supplier emissions, and downstream activities such as product distribution, waste disposal, and employee commuting).

To support this process, Choksi Heraeus Private Limited maintains energy consumption data, production volumes, transport logs, and supplier information. These data points are used to calculate CO₂-equivalent emissions across all scopes. Regular third party carbon audits are performed to monitor emissions trends over time, assess progress toward emission reduction targets, and identify opportunities for further energy efficiency or cleaner technologies. These audits also aid in maintaining regulatory compliance, improving environmental transparency, and guiding sustainability initiatives across operations.

By embedding carbon footprint calculations into its environmental management system, Choksi Heraeus Private Limited strengthens its strategic approach to sustainability and reaffirms its commitment to mitigating climate change.

To ensure systematic assessment and enhancement of energy efficiency across all operations, energy audits will be conducted on a regular basis. These audits will focus on identifying conservation opportunities and improving overall system performance.

substeps.text: Planning and Preparation: An energy audit will be scheduled annually, in coordination with an authorized third-party energy audit firm. Key energy systems and equipment, such as transformers, air compressors, chillers, motors, lighting, and HVAC systems, will be identified in advance for detailed evaluation. The technical and maintenance teams will be notified about the schedule and their roles in supporting data sharing, equipment access, and on-ground coordination. Historical energy data, including electricity bills, operational logs, and equipment specifications, will be compiled to establish baseline performance.

Data Collection and Measurement: Real-time parameters such as voltage, current, power factor, temperature, and load will be measured using calibrated instruments. Energy consumption records for the preceding 12 months will be collected to analyze trends in demand, unit consumption, and billing charges. Details of equipment load, usage hours, operating efficiency, and power system layout will be recorded across departments. Special focus will be given to pumps and motors, as these areas are prone to inefficiencies and energy losses.

Performance Analysis: All measured and recorded data will be analyzed to identify energy losses, low-efficiency equipment, and systems with potential for upgrades. Equipment such as air compressors and chilled water pumps will be evaluated for loading efficiency and specific power consumption. Power quality assessment, including harmonics analysis and power factor checks, will be conducted to evaluate system stability and identify risks of penalties.

Recommendation and Reporting: The audit findings will be compiled into a comprehensive Energy Audit Report, which will include Energy Conservation Measures (EnCon), cost-benefit analysis, estimated savings in kWh and Rupees, and required investment and payback periods.

Implementation and Follow-up: Approved recommendations will be scheduled for phased implementation. The plant team will integrate identified energy-efficient solutions into operations. Post-implementation monitoring will be carried out to compare actual performance against projections. A summary of improvements will be maintained for regulatory compliance, internal review, and continual improvement.

body.text: Purpose: To establish guidelines for the efficient operation and maintenance of the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) followed by Multiple Effect Evaporator (MEE) plant to ensure high recovery of clean water, safe handling of concentrated effluent, compliance with regulatory standards, and minimization of environmental impact. This includes specific measures for the removal of heavy metals from wastewater to safeguard downstream water quality and ensure regulatory compliance.

Operations team, maintenance team, environmental compliance officer, and safety officers conduct daily inspections of the MEE/ETP plants and surrounding areas.
Operators check the availability of utilities (steam, cooling water, power) and ensure feed tanks, pumps, and evaporator sections are in working condition.
Safety officers verify functioning of safety equipment like fire extinguishers, emergency showers, and pressure relief valves..
Feed Monitoring

Influent feed (concentrated wastewater from process streams) is measured for pH, TDS, conductivity, and volume.
Flow meters and level gauges are used to track feed quantity and distribution across evaporator effects.
Evaporation Process

Steam pressure and temperature are monitored at each effect to ensure optimal evaporation and energy efficiency.
Operators record condensate generation, concentration ratio of brine, and steam-to-feed ratio.
Concentrated brine/sludge is safely collected for further treatment or disposal.
Condensate Testing

Condensate samples are collected and tested for pH, conductivity, TDS, silica, and organic load to ensure suitability for reuse or safe discharge.
Non-condensable gases are vented through scrubbers.
Heavy Metal Removal

Concentrated effluent containing heavy metals is collected and directed to a dedicated heavy-metal treatment unit.
Precipitation agents such as saturated lime , and other pH-adjusting chemicals are added in controlled doses.
These reagents convert dissolved heavy metals into insoluble hydroxides or other stable precipitates.
The precipitated particles are removed through sedimentation and subsequent filtration systems to maximize metal removal efficiency.
The sludge generated from heavy-metal removal is dewatered using filter presses or centrifuges to reduce its volume.
Dewatered sludge is stored in leak-proof, labelled containers within a secured hazardous waste storage area.
The sludge is periodically handed over to authorized Hazardous Waste Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities (TSDF) in compliance with statutory requirements.
Treated effluent is tested for parameters such as pH, total dissolved solids, and heavy-metal concentration.
The treated water is recycled back into the industrial process to reduce freshwater use or discharged through approved outlets as per statutory norms.
Performance Monitoring

Key performance indicators such as steam economy, recovery rate, and heat transfer efficiency are recorded daily.
Any deviation (e.g., reduced evaporation rate, scaling, fouling) is reported immediately for corrective action.

The incident is documented, and additional monitoring ensures compliance.

body.text: Containment:

The IT Security Manager will immediately isolate affected systems to prevent further unauthorized access. This could include disconnecting affected systems from the network, disabling user accounts, or restricting access until the issue is resolved.

Communication:

Affected stakeholders will be notified via official email or in person. The communication will explain the nature of the breach, the data affected, and the associated risks. Guidance will include actions to protect their information, such as changing passwords and monitoring for suspicious activities. Updates will be provided regularly.

Management and the legal team will be kept informed through progress updates, emails, meetings, and incident reports. All developments, decisions, and actions are documented and communicated promptly to ensure alignment with Choksi Heraeus Private Limited policies.

Corrective actions will be implemented based on the investigation findings. These include revising data access controls, strengthening encryption protocols, updating security policies, retraining employees, and improving incident detection systems to prevent future breaches.

sops.title: Securing Third-Party Data from Unauthorized Access

blocks.text: To protect sensitive information shared with or received from third parties by implementing strict access controls, ensuring privacy, and minimizing the risk of unauthorized disclosure or data breaches.

body.text:
Access Restrictions: Access to third-party sensitive data is restricted to authorized personnel only, based on their job responsibilities. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is utilized to assign permissions according to specific roles, ensuring that individuals only access the data necessary for their job functions.
Access Reviews: Access permissions are reviewed quarterly by the Data Protection Officer to ensure compliance with data protection policies. Any non-compliance or changes in role will trigger a reassessment of access rights.

Encryption during Transmission: All third-party sensitive data transmitted externally is encrypted using secure protocols such as SSL/TLS to protect the data from unauthorized interception.
Encryption at Rest: Third-party data is encrypted when stored, using industry-standard encryption algorithms like AES-256 to ensure data security even when stored on servers or cloud storage.
Key Management: Encryption keys are stored securely in an access-controlled environment, with access granted on a need-to-know basis only.

Storage Practices: All third-party sensitive data is stored on secure, access-controlled servers, with encryption applied both during storage and transmission. Physical and logical security measures are in place to protect against unauthorized access.
Access Control Reviews: Regular audits and access control reviews are conducted by the IT Security Team to ensure compliance with internal data protection policies, including reviewing logs for unauthorized access attempts and ensuring encryption standards are met.

Secure Sharing: Third-party sensitive data is only shared using secure methods, such as encrypted emails. The identity and authorization of recipients are verified before sharing sensitive data.
Activity Logging: All instances of data sharing are logged, including the recipient's details, the type of data shared, and the time and date of the transaction. These logs are reviewed periodically by the Compliance Team for potential security gaps.

Data Protection Agreements (DPA): All third parties handling or accessing sensitive information are required to sign a Data Protection Agreement (DPA). The DPA outlines the third party's obligations, including security measures and timely reporting of any data breaches.
Contractual Obligations: Contracts with third parties include clauses that mandate the implementation of equivalent security measures and compliance with relevant data protection laws, ensuring that third parties protect the data as diligently as Choksi Heraeus Private Limited.

Regular Training: Employees receive regular training on data protection policies and practices, emphasizing the importance of safeguarding third-party data. The training includes handling procedures, secure sharing methods, and the potential consequences of a data breach.
Role-Specific Training: Employees in roles with direct access to sensitive third-party data receive enhanced training, ensuring they understand their specific responsibilities and how to implement security measures effectively.

Continuous Monitoring: A monitoring system is in place to detect any unauthorized access attempts or unusual access patterns related to third-party data. The IT Security Team conducts real-time monitoring and analysis of network traffic and system logs for potential security incidents.
Regular Audits: Data access logs, storage practices, and third-party compliance with security measures are audited quarterly. These audits are performed by the Compliance and Audit Team, who investigate any discrepancies and report on findings to senior management.

Breach Detection: If a data breach involving third-party information is detected, the Incident Response Team (IRT) follows the established Incident Response Procedure (IRP) to contain and mitigate the breach.
Notification of Affected Parties: Affected third parties are promptly notified, detailing the breach's nature, the data impacted, potential risks, and the steps taken to resolve the incident. Choksi Heraeus Private Limited ensures full transparency in communications and provides guidance on mitigating further risks.
Remediation and Follow-Up: Following the breach, the Data Protection Officer leads efforts to implement corrective actions and improve existing security measures. This includes revising access control measures, enhancing encryption practices, and reviewing third-party agreements to ensure similar incidents do not occur in the future.

Applicability: Third parties with access to sensitive or proprietary information (including production data, client information, and employee data) must undergo information security due diligence.
Initial Assessment: Identify and categorize third parties based on the type of information they will have access to and the potential risk they pose to company information systems.
Third parties will be classified into risk categories based on:

The sensitivity of the data they handle (e.g., Personally Identifiable Information, confidential financial data).
The level of access they have to the company’s systems or infrastructure (e.g., full access vs. limited access).
The location and regulatory environment in which they operate (e.g., regions with strict data protection laws).
Risk Levels:

Low Risk: Third parties with minimal or no access to sensitive data or systems.
Medium Risk: Third parties with restricted access to sensitive data or systems.
High Risk: Third parties with broad or unrestricted access to sensitive data or critical systems.

Initial Evaluation:
Review third-party company profiles, including their information security policies and certifications (e.g., ISO 27001).
Verify their history regarding data breaches, security incidents, and compliance with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA).
Information Security Questionnaire:
Require the third party to complete an information security questionnaire that covers:
Information handling practices.
Security controls (e.g., firewalls, encryption, access management).
Incident response procedures.
Compliance with industry standards (e.g., GDPR).
Screening:
Conduct a screening for any history of security incidents, data breaches, or compliance failures.
Use reputable screening tools or third-party services to verify information.
On-Site Security Audit (for high-risk third parties):
For high-risk third parties, conduct an on-site audit to assess the physical and digital security measures in place.
Verify compliance with agreed-upon security protocols and company standards.

All third-party agreements must include information security clauses that define:
Responsibilities for protecting sensitive data.
Access control measures and limitations.
Rights to audit and inspect security practices.
Notification requirements in the event of a data breach.
Termination clauses in case of security breaches or failure to meet security standards.

Low Risk: Approved by the procurement or department head based on the initial due diligence.
Medium Risk: Requires approval from the Information Security Officer (ISO) and Legal/Compliance team.
High Risk: Final approval by senior management and the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO).

Conduct annual reviews of third-party information security practices.
Continuously monitor third-party activities to ensure compliance with security protocols.
Use automated tools to detect unusual behaviour or potential vulnerabilities in third-party systems.
Follow up on any changes in the third party’s security practices or infrastructure that may affect data security.

narrative.text:
Continuous Monitoring: Use automated monitoring tools to track third-party access to sensitive data and systems.
Periodic Audits: Schedule periodic security audits and vulnerability assessments to verify that third-party security measures remain effective.
Incident Response: If a third-party security breach is identified, the incident response protocol should be activated to mitigate any damage and prevent recurrence.

ISO 27001
Non-compliance by third parties may lead to the termination of business relationships and legal consequences.

responsibilities: Ensure that any third-party engagements requiring access to sensitive information follow the appropriate due diligence process.
Lead the due diligence process for third-party security evaluations, especially for medium- and high-risk vendors.
Oversee the entire due diligence program, especially for high-risk third-party relationships.
Ensure that information security requirements are incorporated into contracts with third parties.
Review contracts to ensure they meet regulatory and security requirements.
Comply with all agreed-upon security standards and participate in regular security reviews and audits.

Changes in regulations or the company’s security needs will be reflected in the SOP to maintain effectiveness.
Updates will be communicated to relevant stakeholders, and training on the revised SOP will be provided as necessary.

sops.title: Audits of Control Procedure to ensure Ethical Compliance

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedure for conducting internal audits at Choksi Heraeus Private Limited to ensure compliance with ethical standards, integrity controls, and responsible business practices across departments. The aim is to proactively detect non-compliance, strengthen accountability, and support a culture of transparency and fair conduct.

Applies to all functional departments at Choksi Heraeus Private Limited, including Finance, Procurement, HR, Marketing, Operations, IT, and Sustainability/Compliance. The procedure also covers controls related to anti-corruption, fair labor practices, responsible sourcing, and financial integrity.

body.text: Audits are conducted annually, and additionally following any major organizational, structural, or regulatory changes.
The Internal Audit Team, in coordination with the Compliance Officer, develops an annual audit calendar with defined scope, objectives, timelines, and responsible persons.

rows: Ensure accuracy of reporting and compliance with internal controls.
Financial records, ledger entries, and financial disclosures.
Verify supplier selection is ethical and fair.
Vendor contracts, tender records, ESG clauses, and sourcing traceability.
Assess compliance with labor laws, fair wages, and non-discrimination.
Hiring records, grievance logs, wage data, and exit interviews.
Validate responsible communication and compliance with branding ethics.
Advertising materials, digital campaigns, and buyer-facing collateral.
Evaluate adherence to SOPs and ethical work environment standards.
SOP implementation, resource management, and incident logs.
Assess systems for secure handling of sensitive and supplier data.
Access controls, cybersecurity protocols, data protection practices.
Detect bribery risks and corruption vulnerabilities.
Gifts/hospitality logs, whistleblower cases, Code of Conduct adherence.

body.text:
The Audit Team reviews documentation and digital records associated with each area: including contracts, logs, approvals, training records, and incident reports.
Reviews are conducted against Choksi Heraeus Private Limited Ethical Code of Conduct, Supplier Code, Labor Compliance Framework, and relevant local regulations.
Interviews with key employees and department leads are conducted to validate processes and uncover hidden gaps or informal practices.

Quantitative and qualitative data are analyzed to identify trends, irregularities, and early indicators of non-compliance.
Internal benchmarks (e.g., labor compliance rate, supplier grievance rate, wage audit compliance %) are used for performance comparison.
Ethical risk scoring may be applied for departments or suppliers with prior compliance issues.
A detailed Ethical Compliance Audit Report is prepared after each audit, containing:

Summary of observations
List of non-conformities
Root cause analysis (if applicable)
Recommendations for process and control improvement
Reports are submitted to senior management, and relevant department heads within 10 business days of audit completion.
A Corrective Action Plan (CAP) is formulated in coordination with each audited department, detailing:

Action items
Target completion dates
Accountable persons

The Compliance Department schedules follow-up audits or spot checks to verify the implementation and effectiveness of corrective actions.
Recurring non-compliances are escalated to top management and included in performance evaluations.

rows.record: Audit materials (plans, checklists, reports, CAPs, and follow-up findings)

blocks.text:
All audit materials (plans, checklists, reports, CAPs, and follow-up findings) are stored securely, both digitally and in hard copy where needed.
The Audit Team, in coordination with the Compliance Department, maintains these records for a minimum of 5 years for internal reviews or third-party audits.

sections.title: Review and Improvement of Audit Mechanism

blocks.text:
This SOP is reviewed annually by the compliance manager to incorporate changes in legal frameworks, buyer codes of conduct, or Choksi’s own ethical standards.
Lessons learned from each audit cycle are used to update checklists, risk indicators, and training content to improve future compliance.
